title: When the Vector Burns
premise: Astrid Halloran tends the last living garden on Kepler Station, a terraforming outpost whose human founders are long dead, leaving only automated systems and a beacon no one remembers commissioning. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Astrid discovers the beacon has been translating and rebroadcasting Earth's final transmission loop for generations — and that two warring colony fleets have each claimed the message as divine sanction. To end the war, Astrid must deliver the true, uncorrupted message to both fleets before the loop decays forever, knowing the truth will shatter one side's founding myth and possibly ignite the very war it could end. In the end, Astrid chooses to broadcast the truth in the extinct language itself — forcing both fleets to learn it together to understand — buying peace at the cost of the garden, the station, and Astrid's own place in history.
about_author: Ada Ravensworth is the pen name of a former botanist who spent six years cataloguing seed vaults in remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write about lonely outposts, inherited machines, and the messages we leave for strangers.

chapters.title: The Garden of the Unborn
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet them tending the terraforming garden on near-empty Kepler Station, speaking aloud to plants meant for colonists who may never come. The chapter establishes their ritual, isolation, and quiet devotion to a purpose they didn't choose. Emotional beat: tender loneliness, the dignity of caretaking without an audience.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The station's ancient receiver catches a distress call in Pre-Collapse Standard, a language extinct for two centuries. Astrid realizes they can almost read it — and that the beacon they've maintained for years is transmitting something far older than anyone knew. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with the beacon's archived logs as interludes. Digging into the station's corrupted archives, Astrid learns the beacon has been looping Earth's final transmission for 200 years — and that someone deliberately scrambled its origin records. Emotional beat: betrayal across time; the past was edited on purpose.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Commander Sefa Idris of the Ashfall Fleet and Captain Yorick Vane of the Meridian Compact, locked in a three-year war over shipping lanes, each citing 'the Earth Message' as proof of their mandate. Neither knows the other's copy is corrupted differently. Emotional beat: righteous conviction on both sides, dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A damaged Ashfall scout crashes near Kepler Station; Astrid saves the pilot, Lieutenant Okonkwo, who recognizes fragments of the dead language from her grandmother's forbidden songs. She becomes Astrid's first ally — and first witness. Emotional beat: cautious trust blooming between strangers.

chapters.title: Decay
chapters.summary: Astrid and Okonkwo's shared POV chapters. The transmission loop is degrading; within weeks the original message will be unrecoverable. They reconstruct it piece by piece and discover its content is neither fleet's founding myth — it's a confession and a warning. Emotional beat: urgency, grief, the weight of knowing.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The Compact intercepts word of Kepler Station's discovery and moves to seize or destroy it, believing the truth will dissolve his people's legitimacy. Vane confronts his own corruption: he's known his copy was altered for years. Emotional beat: a man choosing the lie because the lie holds his world together.

chapters.title: Burn the Vector
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Both fleets converge on Kepler Station. Astrid must choose: transmit the truth to one side and hand them a weapon, destroy the beacon and bury the message forever, or find a third path. The garden burns in the crossfire. Emotional beat: devastating loss; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: A Language Worth Learning
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. Astrid broadcasts the true message in extinct Pre-Collapse Standard — intelligible only if both fleets' linguists work together, using Okonkwo's grandmother's songs as the key. Decoding becomes cooperation; the war pauses mid-battle as enemies translate side by side. Emotional beat: transcendent unity forged through shared effort.

chapters.title: Seeds for Strangers
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV, epilogue. A year later, the ceasefire holds, fragile but real. Kepler Station is a memorial; its surviving seed vault is distributed to both fleets' generation ships. Astrid, unrecognized by choice, plants a new garden aboard a joint vessel. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope — survival was paid for, and what grows next belongs to everyone.
